title: The Cold Lamp

where.detail: a frozen stream running up into the forest from the Wend, a little north of where the company crossed

time: the first morning across the Wend
last_beat: Rae walked the cart up onto the frozen stream into the forest by her grandmother's way, and Darrow came last, with the cold lamp behind them and its black chip turning on its thong in no wind at all.

people.did: Looked back at the five horses on the far bank and the smoke over the reeds; knew the black chip on the lamp-post for the kind of thing he had seen under a lad's tongue; asked Rae which way, and followed.
people.now: Going up a frozen stream into the Thornwild at the back of the company, with Wren.

facts.fact: He put aside the urge to take the obvious line first and asked Rae which way to go.
facts.evidence: He looked at Rae instead.

facts.fact: He saw that the black chip on the lamp-post was like the one taken from under the tongue of the lad in the Grey Cot, scorched.
facts.evidence: He had seen a thing like it once before, no bigger than a barleycorn

people.did: Stopped Wren touching what hung on the lamp; named the wood with her grandmother's word, greth; took the company in by her grandmother's way, up a frozen stream.
people.now: Leading the cart up the frozen stream into the forest, by her grandmother's way.

facts.fact: She told Wren you don't touch what's hung on a lamp, not here.
facts.evidence: "You don't touch what's hung on a lamp," Rae said. "Not here."

facts.fact: Her grandmother's word for the country east of the river is greth, the grey country, and Rae said her gran would not have liked her saying it there.
facts.evidence: "She'd not have liked me saying it here."

facts.fact: Her grandmother came out of the forest by a frozen stream the year she came over, and Rae took the company in by it, knowing it only as her gran had told it.
facts.evidence: "I know the way she told it."

people.did: Noticed there were no bells; reached for the chip on the lamp-post and was stopped.
people.now: Going up the frozen stream at the back with Darrow.

facts.fact: She noticed first that there are no bells in the Thornwild.
facts.evidence: "There's no bell," Wren said.

people.did: Looked at the black chip on the lamp-post with the face she has for a wound.
people.now: Walking at the cart's tail up the frozen stream.

facts.fact: She looked at the black chip the way she looks at a wound before she touches it.
facts.evidence: her face had the look it got at a wound before she touched it.

people.did: Asked whose door the lamp marked; swore at the stream's angle from the tailboard.
people.now: On the tailboard of Rae's cart going up the frozen stream.

people.did: Stood at the forest's edge with her nose working and her tail going round, then ranged ahead.
people.now: Ranging ahead up the frozen stream.

codex.name: Greth
codex.text: Rae's grandmother's word, said from the belly: the grey country east of the river (Ch 8 Sc 1).

codex.name: The clans' lamps
codex.text: An iron lamp on a post at the edge of the Thornwild, shuttered on three sides and open to the river, with a scorched black chip tied below it on a thong; a lamp at every door, Rae's grandmother said, and a door is anywhere they say it is (Ch 8 Sc 1).

struggle: The forest across the river, and whatever it is full of.

now.against: A forest with no bells, and lamps nobody has lit.
now.next: Up the frozen stream into the Thornwild by Rae's grandmother's way.

title: Bread on a Stump

where.detail: a camp in the lee of the stream bank, within sight of a lit lamp-post, a day up the frozen stream

time: the first full day up the stream, the night, and the next morning
last_beat: In the morning the loaf on the stump was gone, and the red cloth with it; in the snow beside the stump there was one ski-track, coming and going.

people.did: Walked a day beside a watch he could not see; when Ash ate the bread left at a lit lamp, put down the urge to follow the ski-tracks and let Rae say what went down in its place; at dusk the script changed on his palms and he told Wren first.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp, a day up the stream, the script on his hands changed.

facts.fact: He wanted to follow the ski-tracks and apologise to the watch himself, and let Rae set the price instead.
facts.evidence: "It's your gran's word," he said. "You say what goes down."

facts.fact: The word under his name on the script changed, and it sits lower and steadier on his palms, like something tempered.
facts.evidence: The word under his name had changed.

facts.fact: He told Wren first what the script said, before anyone.
facts.evidence: "You're the first. Nobody else has it."

facts.fact: The third finger of his right hand, white after the ring, has come back; the two slow ones have not.
facts.evidence: the third beside them that had come back to him since the ring

people.did: Named tal when Ash ate the bread at the lamp; set down one of the millers' loaves on the red cloth, bread for bread; banked the fire with her three turns.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: Tal, her grandmother's word: a gift laid down at a door before you ask anything of the house, or the asking is an insult.
facts.evidence: "It was a gift laid down before an ask."

facts.fact: She paid back the eaten bread with one of the miller's wife's loaves, bread for bread, same size or bigger, as her grandmother taught her.
facts.evidence: "Bread for bread," she said. "Same size or bigger. That's what she taught me."

facts.fact: She banks the fire with the same three turns of a stick every night and will not say where she learned them.
facts.evidence: Rae banked it with three turns of a stick, the same three as every night

people.did: Offered a pencil for the gift; sat by Darrow at the fire and was told first what the script said; wrote it in two places.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp with the ledger.

facts.fact: When he told her first what the script said, she wrote one under her sum and Five under Told first.
facts.evidence: and wrote *Five.*, and drew a line under it

people.did: Offered a knife and thought better of it; went still at singing in the trees, a tune he half knows, and would not say from where.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: He half knows the tune sung in the trees at night, and would not say from where.
facts.evidence: "No," said Hollis. He put the cup down. "Half of it."

people.did: Would not give her salt, which is for wounds; looked at his foot at the fire, as every night since the mill, and called it pink.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: She would not give her salt as the gift; it is for wounds.
facts.evidence: "Not my salt. That salt's for wounds."

facts.fact: At the fire she looked at his right foot, as every night since the mill, and gave it its first good word: pink.
facts.evidence: "Pink," she said: the first good word she had given it.

people.did: Ate the bread left on the stump at the lit lamp, and brought Darrow the cloth.
people.now: At the camp by the lit lamp.

facts.fact: She ate the bread laid down at a clan lamp in front of everyone.
facts.evidence: with the red cloth in her mouth and crumbs in her beard

codex.name: Tal
codex.text: Rae's grandmother's word: a gift laid down at a door before you ask anything of the house; without it the asking is an insult. Bread for bread, same size or bigger (Ch 8 Sc 2).

struggle: A watch he cannot see, and a door he has wronged without knowing it.

now.against: A watch that walks beside them unseen.

title: Their Road

where.detail: on the frozen stream at dusk, running for the clans' lamp line a mile ahead, out in front of the company

time: dusk, the second day up the stream
last_beat: Ahead of all of them on the ice, with the cart falling behind and the clans' lamps standing across the stream a mile off, he was the fastest thing on the river.

people.did: Asked Rae how far to the horn and ran for the lamps on the stream ice, straight and not fast, and within two hundred strides was ahead of everyone.
people.now: Running on the stream ice at dusk with a lamp and the stick, ahead of the whole company, the clans' lamps a mile off and the cart falling behind him.

facts.fact: On the flat ice, running straight and not fast, he outran the whole company within two hundred strides.
facts.evidence: Within another hundred the oxen's breathing had gone behind him, and then the bell.

people.did: Turned the watch's shouted word into Vaelish, run; read that every track crossed the stream and none walked it, said once that she had brought them up their road, and drove the oxen at a trot.
people.now: Running at Hob's head with the cart at an ox-trot, a long way behind Darrow.

facts.fact: She knew the word the watch shouted down through the trees: run.
facts.evidence: "Run," she said, in plain Vaelish, to all of them. "It means run."

facts.fact: She believes her grandmother's way up the stream is the road the thing in the trees walks, and said so once.
facts.evidence: "It's their road. I brought you up their road."

people.did: Called himself luggage with opinions; hauled Maelis up onto the tailboard; held a lamp up behind the cart toward what was coming, and shouted at the Captain to run on and bang on the clans' door.
people.now: On the tailboard among the flour sacks with Maelis, holding a lamp up behind the cart.

facts.fact: He shouted at Darrow to go on ahead to the clans' door, the only one of them they would open it for.
facts.evidence: You're the only one of us they'll open it for—

people.did: Was hauled onto the tailboard by Hollis, roll and all; told Darrow, on the ice, straight.
people.now: On the tailboard with Hollis as the cart runs.

people.did: Counted the watch's lamps along the ridge; lit Rae's three lamps on the ice, swearing at the flint, gave Darrow one and hung one on the cart.
people.now: Running on the ice between the cart and Darrow with a lamp.

people.did: Turned to face back down the stream and growled without stopping; ran back and forth between Darrow and the cart.
people.now: Running between Darrow and the cart, unable to choose.

codex.name: The watch's horn
codex.text: Two notes, the second lower and longer, sounded at dusk from up the frozen stream in the Thornwild where the clans' lamps came down across the ice. Not a bell (Ch 8 Sc 3).

add: a lit lamp off Rae's cord, in his right hand

now.against: Something slow and many coming up the stream behind them at a walk, and the cart falling behind.
now.next: Where Darrow runs on the ice, and who reaches the lamps first.

title: Whose Dog

where.detail: inside the clans' lamp line across the frozen stream, by the watch's fire

time: nightfall, the second day up the stream
last_beat: The watch's leader ruled that the dog may stay and the Vaelmark walk back to the river at first light; asked if that meant all of them, Rae said: "He said the Vaelmark. That's us."

people.did: Dropped back to run at the cart's tail beside Hollis; laughed back out loud when the watch laughed at his running; tried to make their leader hear him in plain Vaelish, was heard out, and was sent back to the river.
people.now: Inside the clans' lamp line at nightfall, let in by nobody, to walk back down the stream to the river at first light.

facts.fact: When the watch laughed at his running, he laughed back, out loud.
facts.evidence: So he laughed back.

facts.fact: He told the watch's leader in plain Vaelish who they were and that what they carried would not keep, and the leader understood none of it.
facts.evidence: So he said it himself.

people.did: Spoke for the company with her few clan words; gave the dog's new name; stopped Wren asking what was in the trees; carried the leader's ruling, and counted herself among the Vaelmark sent home.
people.now: At the watch's fire inside the lamp line, to go back down the stream with the company at first light.

facts.fact: She has only a handful of words of the clans' tongue.
facts.evidence: "I've seven words of theirs," said Rae.

facts.fact: Her grandmother taught her that the thing in the trees is not named at night.
facts.evidence: "You don't name it at night. Gran said."

facts.fact: She counted herself among the Vaelmark the watch sent back to the river.
facts.evidence: "He said the Vaelmark," she said. "That's us."

people.did: Rode the tailboard with the lamp held out behind; told Darrow the watch now thought him simple; took the ruling as second to the dog.
people.now: On the tailboard by the watch's fire inside the lamp line.

facts.fact: He took the watch's ruling as a joke against the company.
facts.evidence: "Second to the dog," he said. "I've served under worse."

people.did: Got down and read the knee on the tailboard in front of the watch after the run.
people.now: By the watch's fire inside the lamp line.

facts.fact: After his run on the stream ice she read the knee and found it had held.
facts.evidence: "It held," she said, and gave him back his leg.

people.did: Counted the watch, twelve and the horn; asked Rae what was in the trees and was stopped.
people.now: By the watch's fire inside the lamp line, with her lamp.

people.did: Was looked over, fed and admired by the watch, took their meat only from Darrow's left hand, and was named a watcher.
people.now: Following the watch's leader across the ice for what else is in his pouch.

facts.fact: The clans' watch named her corr, a watcher.
facts.evidence: "*Corr*," said Rae. "The heron. They call a watcher that."

codex.name: Corr
codex.text: The clans' word for the heron, and so for a watcher: what the watch at the lamp line called Ash, with a hand on her head, after she turned to the trees before anyone (Ch 8 Sc 4).

codex.name: The watch at the lamp line
codex.text: A dozen of the clans on skis, furred to the eyes, with a torch in one hand and a long spear in the other; at night they set a line of lamps across the frozen stream and hold it, spears turned outward, until the trees are quiet. Their leader carries the horn (Ch 8 Sc 4).

fired.evidence: he fell in beside it and ran there, at the back, the last of them

now.against: The watch has ruled the Vaelmark back down the stream at first light; the dog may stay.
now.next: First light, and the road back down to the river.

title: Oddny of Haskel

where.detail: on a forest track toward the clans' holdfast at dusk, under the watch's guard, with lamps ahead

time: the third day across the Wend, first light to dusk
last_beat: Walking at Hob's head with her goad in his hand, he told Rae he would have walked back; she said, "I know. That's why I didn't ask."

people.did: Asked Rae to have the watch take her in alone and send the rest back; let her spend her grandmother's name without stopping her; saw the chips at every throat and the burned clearing; was looked at too long by the leader; carried Rae's goad at dusk.
people.now: Under the watch's guard on a forest track at dusk, beside Rae at Hob's head with her goad in his hand, with the lamps of a holdfast ahead.

facts.fact: He asked Rae to have the watch take her in alone and send the rest of them back to the river.
facts.evidence: Ask him to take you in, you and the cart, and send the rest of us down to the river.

facts.fact: The watch's leader looked at him a long time, then closed a hand in the air at the height of a man's collar and pulled, and Darrow remembered being hauled out of the ford.
facts.evidence: closed it in the air at the height of a man's collar, and pulled

people.did: Stopped the column and said her grandmother's name to the watch's leader, and her own after it in the clans' way; the watch turned from the river toward the holdfast.
people.now: At Hob's head on the track toward the holdfast, under guard; what spending her grandmother's name has cost her she does not yet know.

facts.fact: Her grandmother was Oddny of Haskel.
facts.evidence: "Oddny of Haskel."

facts.fact: She named herself to the watch in the clans' way as Oddny's granddaughter, and it turned them from sending the company back.
facts.evidence: "Rae. Of Oddny. Of Haskel."

facts.fact: She spent her grandmother's name without asking Darrow, because she knew he would have walked back.
facts.evidence: "I know," said Rae. "That's why I didn't ask."

people.did: Rode the tailboard and said he had been thrown out of many places and never a wood.
people.now: On the tailboard, under guard.

facts.fact: He says he has been thrown out of alehouses, a brothel in Calden and once a chapel.
facts.evidence: Alehouses. A brothel in Calden. A chapel, once, which wasn't my fault.

people.did: Saw the black chips at the watch's throats and kept her hand flat over the linen in her coat for a mile.
people.now: Walking with the cart under guard.

people.did: Asked who Oddny was; counted the chips, fourteen; looked once at the burned clearing and stopped counting.
people.now: Walking with the cart under guard.

people.did: Slept under the leader's furs; walked at the head with him and came back to Darrow every mile.
people.now: With the column, between the leader and Darrow.

codex.name: Oddny of Haskel
codex.text: Rae Thorne's grandmother, Thornwild-born, who came over the Wend behind a Lowmarch drover; Rae named herself to the clans' watch as hers, in the clans' way: Rae, of Oddny, of Haskel (Ch 8 Sc 5).

codex.name: The chips at the throat
codex.text: Every one of the clans' watch wears a black glassy chip no bigger than a thumbnail on a thong at the throat, like the one on the cold lamp at the river; their leader wears two (Ch 8 Sc 5).

codex.name: The burned clearing
codex.text: A clearing in the Thornwild as wide as a threshing floor, black at the middle and ringed with charred stakes, with a sleeve of mail fused in the ash and a greasy smell the frost has not got out; the watch go round it the long way with their eyes down (Ch 8 Sc 5).

remove: a lit lamp off Rae's cord, in his right hand

now.against: Under guard toward a holdfast that has granted a hearing and nothing more; what Rae's name has cost her is not yet known.
now.next: The holdfast's lamps, and the hearing.

title: A Gift Before the Ask

where.detail: outside the gate of a clan holdfast at night, by a basket of coals under the gate lamp

time: full dark, the third day across the Wend, snow falling
last_beat: Rae told him the gift was his to give; the old woman on her stool folded her hands and waited, with every face on the wall waiting with her.

people.did: Said tal to the holdfast's elder, from the nose and then from the belly; took stock of the little the company had; remembered a clan boy he killed at another ford; asked Rae what her grandmother would have laid down.
people.now: Outside the holdfast gate at night by the watch's coals, with the elder waiting for the gift that must come before the ask.

facts.fact: Years ago, at another ford, he killed a clan boy with a boar spear and had to put a boot on his shoulder to work the lance free.
facts.evidence: a boy with a boar spear too long for him had come at Thistle's chest out of the shallows

facts.fact: He believes the clans owe him nothing but a grave.
facts.evidence: These people owed him nothing. A grave, perhaps.

people.did: Carried the elder's question; taught him to say tal from the belly; told him this gift was his to give.
people.now: Outside the holdfast gate with the company, under the old woman's eye.

facts.fact: She holds that a gift is from the one who asks, and that her grandmother's name was hers.
facts.evidence: "I've given mine. This one's yours."

people.did: Was counted as half a man by a child on the wall, and was delighted; told Darrow not to give the sword.
people.now: On the tailboard outside the holdfast gate, gone still.

facts.fact: He will not have the Captain's sword given to the clans.
facts.evidence: "Not the sword," Hollis said. "Not here. Not to them."

people.did: Untied the salt she keeps for wounds and offered it as the gift.
people.now: By the coals outside the holdfast gate.

facts.fact: She offered her wound salt for the clans' gift, because they would have wounds.
facts.evidence: "They'll have wounds," she said.

people.did: Counted the children on the wall back, Vaelish against clan; hid her ledger in her coat; warned Darrow that the clans sing about the ford.
people.now: At Darrow's elbow outside the holdfast gate.

facts.fact: She warned Darrow that the clans sing about the ford, and Hollis knows half the song.
facts.evidence: They sing about the ford. Hollis knows half the song.

people.did: Was counted twice by the children on the wall, once from each end.
people.now: Outside the holdfast gate with the company.

codex.name: The holdfast at the valley's head
codex.text: A clan holdfast at the head of a valley in the Thornwild: a wall of whole trunks with the bark on, set upright and sharpened, higher than a mounted man; a lamp beside every door and a bigger one at the gate. Its old are carried out on the backs of the young (Ch 8 Sc 6).

now.against: A gift must come before the ask at a door whose people have every reason to want him dead.
now.next: What Darrow lays down at the holdfast gate.
